subject: Production degradation at VaultBank — reserved throughput shortfall & escalation
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@vaultbank.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors & sharp latency spike — urgent

Hi Ben,

We started seeing a sustained latency and error-rate increase across our payments reconciliation calls at ~07:40 PST. Token throughput is dropping and multiple jobs are timing out — our ops team is seeing 500s that map back to token queueing on your reserved cluster. This is impacting end-of-day close for a handful of merchant batches.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a dedicated pool saturation issue or a routing shortfall? We need a clear ETA on mitigation and whether this will affect our SLA credits / auto-fallback. Procurement also copied for context on any short-term capacity add.

Attached are a couple of snippets from our logs (we redacted PII). Happy to jump on an emergency call.

—Tom Reyes
Head of Platform Reliability, VaultBank
Attachments: vaultbank_ops_excerpt.log (text)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & sharp latency spike — urgent

Tom — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I’m pulling the team together now.

Immediate notes:
- We are seeing signs consistent with a reserved throughput shortfall on the dedicated pool serving VaultBank (token queue depth up, per-GPU utility spiking).
- I’m elevating to engineering: Vivek (serving) and Prio (deployment/po) are on the thread.
- Will propose short-term mitigations (traffic shaping + model-variant fallback) and an exec huddle to discuss capacity.

Can you confirm the highest priority routes (API keys or route IDs) to isolate traffic? That will speed mitigations.

Ben Carter
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & sharp latency spike — urgent

Adding quick diagnostics from runtime:
- Observed: sustained 95th percentile token latency went from ~120ms -> ~540ms for VaultBank routes starting at 07:35 PST.
- GPU metrics: one dedicated pool (pool-id dp-vault-01) is at 93% GPU SM utilization, KV cache growth higher than normal, and queue depth per-worker > expected threshold.
- Allocation: VaultBank is pinned to reserved throughput of 1.2M tokens/min. Current demand spiked to ~1.9M tokens/min across the observed window.

Short-term mitigation options (fast -> slower):
1) Prefix-based traffic shaping (rate-limits) at LB for lowest-risk routes — we can deploy in ~10–15m.
2) Route-level fallback to a smaller quantized model variant for non-sensitive flows — 20–30m if we already have the variant on the same pool.
3) Temporary cross-pool burst (borrow capacity from sibling dedicated pools) — requires exec approval + billing override; ETA 45m to bring up and verify.
4) Immediate 30% token-throttle per-key (aggressive) — mitigates load but will raise client error/ retry handling work.

I’ll attach the perf snapshot and a quick heatmap to the thread. Vivek
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & sharp latency spike — urgent

Thanks Vivek — good clear options. Quick commercial notes for the customer:
- If we need immediate cross-pool burst (option 3), we should offer a temporary emergency credit for any overage while we stand up the extra capacity — keeps VaultBank whole for merchant SLA exposure.
- If the fallback model (option 2) is acceptable for reconciliation non-sensitive endpoints, propose running it for the next 24 hours while we stabilize capacity.

Requesting an exec huddle (Ben will lead) to decide. Ben: can you loop in the on-call infra lead (Prio) and an exec from Revenue Ops? I’ll prepare suggested credit language and a short remediation timeline for the customer.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production errors & sharp latency spike — urgent

Planning an exec huddle in 20 minutes to decide on burst + credits. Agenda:
- Confirm observability numbers (Vivek)
- Impact assessment and list of affected routes (Ben)
- Remediation options + rollout plan (Prio)
- Commercial remediation (Marissa)

Tom — we’re lining up an action plan and will confirm the immediate step in the huddle. If you can share the route IDs for the highest-throughput keys before 09:30 PST that will help us target throttles/fallback.

Also looping Irene for legal/contract implications on automatic crediting.

—Ben
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@vaultbank.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-huddle summary and actions (VaultBank incident)

Summary from the 09:40 huddle and follow-ups:
- Immediate action taken (09:50 PST): applied conservative prefix rate-limit for three noisy routes; deployed quantized fallback (gptq-variant) for reconciliation-read-only endpoints. Early telemetry shows 95p latency dropped to ~180ms and error rate down 80%.
- Emergency burst approved by Revenue Ops and Finance for 3 hours to run cross-pool capacity (dp-burst-01). Capacity onlined at ~10:35 PST; full verification completed at 10:55 PST.
- Commercial remediation: Marissa drafted a one-time emergency credit equal to estimated incremental cost for the burst. Irene will sign off on wording; we will include a 2-week post-incident SLA report.
- Next steps: engineering to investigate root cause (traffic sudden spike vs misestimated token mix). Action owners: Vivek (root cause), Prio (safeguards for auto-burst), Marissa (customer comms & credit), Ben (exec wrap-up).

Attachments: reserved_throughput_snapshot_20280323.png, vaultbank_sla_errors_20280323.pdf

Priyo Das
Principal, Customer Reliability Operations, Redwood Inference
